This model describes methanol synthesis from hydrogen, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide over a commercial copper/zinc oxide/alumina catalyst in a differential CSTR. It predicts gas composition and methanol production while tracking changes in the fraction of reduced catalyst surface centers, which affect the activity of the different reactions. The simplified model combines lumped Langmuir–Hinshelwood rate expressions and algebraic surface coverages with dynamic balances for the catalyst and reactor. It was fitted and tested against 140 steady-state experiments and feed-switching experiments

The simplified steady-state-φ model describes methanol synthesis from hydrogen and CO and/or CO₂ over a Cu/ZnO/Al₂O₃ catalyst, predicting reaction rates and gas composition. It uses lumped Langmuir–Hinshelwood kinetics and distinguishes oxidized and reduced catalyst surface centers, with their relative amounts calculated from an equilibrium morphology relation. The authors fitted its kinetic parameters to 140 steady-state experiments in a differential Micro-Berty reactor, spanning feeds from pure CO to pure CO₂.
